Phoneme-ASR spike v2 — Whisper + espeak BP G2P

ASR openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo → text → phonemizer/espeak-ng pt-br → BP IPA · 21 word clips · audio players embedded base64.

TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY OK. GOOD clips reproduce 100% of their BP markers. But Whisper is word-aware — on a mispronounced clip it can rescue the intended word and produce canonical IPA anyway, masking the defect. Use as a transcription-quality check, not a true acoustic gate.
How this differs from spike v1 (wav2vec2-espeak)

v1 was acoustic. The wav2vec2-espeak model emitted IPA directly from raw audio — what the model literally heard. It was EP-biased: even on confirmed-GOOD BP clips it stripped the BP palatalization (dʒ→d, tʃ→t) and the final-i raising (i→ɨ). Useful in principle as a defect detector, but unreliable enough on good clips that you can't separate signal from noise.

v2 is two-stage. Whisper-large-v3-turbo transcribes the audio to BP text — this is the strongest open BP ASR available. Then espeak-ng's pt-br voice phonemizes that text to IPA. The IPA now comes from a deterministic rule-based BP phonemizer, not a potentially-biased acoustic model — so on good audio the output matches the Stage-5 reference almost exactly.

The trade-off

Whisper hears words, not phonemes. On a mispronounced clip Whisper can still recognize the intended word — and then espeak emits the textbook BP IPA, which matches the reference, which makes the clip look fine even though it isn't. This pipeline can only flag clips that confuse Whisper enough to produce wrong text (e.g. sede → 'Cd', de → 'Dio'). Cleanly mispronounced clips the recognizer can still parse correctly — like a soft-EP verde — will pass through silently.

How to read each card

  1. reference IPA — the textbook BP pronunciation from Stage 5.
  2. Whisper heard (text) — exactly what Whisper transcribed.
  3. espeak pt-br IPA — Whisper's text run through espeak's BP phonemizer, normalized to Stage-5 convention (y→i, x→ʁ, lj→ʎ, etc.).
  4. Compare the reference IPA to the espeak IPA. On a GOOD clip they should be near-identical. Big divergence ⇒ Whisper failed to transcribe, which itself is a defect signal.

GOOD 100% vs human-BAD 83%, gap +17%, v3 Gemini-BAD 75%. A small gap here is the expected outcome for a transcription-quality pipeline — Whisper recovers the intended word on most BAD clips too, so their IPA also matches the reference. The useful signal is the absolute level on GOOD clips (is the transcription faithful?) plus the cases where Whisper fails to transcribe at all (a defect signal).
